author: Forster, 1772

art.subject: White-crowned Sparrow (Zonotrichia leucophrys), adult in winter, a vagrant in Korean farmland hedgerows: crown boldly striped black and white — a broad white central stripe between black lateral stripes; a white supercilium; a black stripe behind the eye, the lores pale grey as in the Alaskan form gambelii; face, neck, throat and breast plain grey; belly whitish, flanks buff-brown; mantle brown with dark streaks and greyish edges; wings brown with two white wing bars; tail long and plain brown. Bill pinkish-orange; eye dark; legs pinkish.
art.pose: foraging on the ground beside a hedge, side view
art.scene: hedgerow and weedy field margin in Korean farmland in winter (December–February), soft winter light; no people, buildings or text
art.build: A large, long-tailed American sparrow, clearly larger and longer than a House Sparrow, with a slightly peaked crown, upright stance and long tail; feeds on the ground near cover. Bill conical, small for the bird's size, shorter than the head. Legs pinkish, medium length. The long tail extends well beyond the wingtips; tail plain brown, slightly rounded, without white.
avoid: Do not paint a yellow spot in front of the eye or a white throat patch — that is White-throated Sparrow.
Do not paint a yellow crown patch (Golden-crowned Sparrow).
Do not paint a dark bill; it is pinkish-orange.
Do not streak the grey breast.
Do not paint black lores; in gambelii the black eye-line starts behind the eye.
